'''Juan Ignacio Cirac Sasturain''' (born 11 October 1965),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Ignacio Cirac |url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/ignacio-cirac |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=www.mpq.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref> known professionally as '''Ignacio Cirac''', is a Spanish [[physicist]]. He is one of the pioneers of the field of [[quantum computing]] and [[quantum information]] theory. He was awarded the 2013 [[Wolf Prize in Physics]].

== Early life and education ==
Juan Ignacio Cirac Sasturain{{cn|date=December 2024}}  graduated from the [[Complutense University of Madrid]] in 1988.{{cn|date=December 2024}} 

==Career==
Cirac moved to the United States in 1991 to work as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral scientist]] with [[Peter Zoller]] in the [[Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics]] in [[University of Colorado at Boulder]]. Between 1991 and 1996, he was teaching physics in the Ciudad Real Faculty of Chemistry, University of Castilla-La Mancha.<ref name="CV-leopoldina">{{cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Cirac_Ignacio-DE.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae |website=leopoldina.org |editor=[[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]]|access-date=21 January 2018}}</ref>

In 1996, Cirac became professor in the Institut für Theoretische Physik in [[Innsbruck]], Austria, and in 2001 he became a director of the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] in [[Garching]], Germany, where he heads{{when|date=December 2024}} the Theory Division. At the same time, he was appointed [[Honorary title (academic)|honorary professor]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]]. 

He is a distinguished visiting professor and research advisor at [[ICFO]] – the Institute of Photonic Sciences in [[Barcelona]] since its foundation in 2002. He has been a member of research teams at the universities of [[Harvard University|Harvard]], [[Technical University of Munich]], [[University of Hamburg|Hamburg]], [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UCSB]], [[University of Hannover|Hannover]], [[University of Bristol|Bristol]], [[University of Paris|Paris]], [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre|CEA/Saclay]], [[École Normale Supérieure]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="pda2006">{{cite web |url=http://www.fpa.es/en/princess-of-asturias-awards/laureates/2006-juan-ignacio-cirac.html?texto=trayectoria&especifica=0 |title=Juan Ignacio Cirac: Prince of Asturias Award for Technical & Scientific Research 2006 |publisher=Fundación Princesa de Asturias |website=fpa.es |access-date=21 January 2018 |archive-date=28 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181028225709/http://www.fpa.es/en/princess-of-asturias-awards/laureates/2006-juan-ignacio-cirac.html?texto=trayectoria&especifica=0 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His research is focused on [[quantum optics]], the quantum theory of information, and quantum many-body physics. His joint work with Peter Zoller on ion trap quantum computation opened up the possibility of experimental quantum computation, and his joint work on optical lattices jumpstarted the field of quantum simulation. He has also made seminal contributions in the fields of quantum information theory, degenerated quantum gases, quantum optics, and renormalization group methods.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/8281/ |title=Member's Profile |website=leopoldina.org |editor=[[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]] German Academy of Sciences |access-date=21 January 2018}}</ref> As of 2017 Juan Ignacio Cirac has published more than 440 articles in the most prestigious journals<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www2.mpq.mpg.de/Theorygroup/CIRAC/wiki/images/5/5d/J_Ignacio_Cirac_CV_2017_December.pdf |title=Resume – Juan Ignacio Cirac |publisher=MPI for Quantum Optics |access-date=21 January 2018 |archive-date=22 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180122072512/http://www2.mpq.mpg.de/Theorygroup/CIRAC/wiki/images/5/5d/J_Ignacio_Cirac_CV_2017_December.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and is one of the most cited authors in his fields of research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.webometrics.info/es/node/58 |publisher=webometrics.info |title=2258 Highly Cited Researchers (h>100) according to their Google Scholar Citations public profiles |access-date=21 January 2018}} (Cirac is no. 592 on the list)</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://clarivate.com/hcr/2017-researchers-list/#freeText%3DCirac |publisher=clarivate.com |title=2017 Highly Cited Researchers |access-date=21 January 2018}}</ref> He has been named among others as a possible candidate to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/nobel-prize-sizzle-building-excitement-in-the-run-up-to-the-physics-award/ |title=Nobel prize sizzle: building excitement in the run-up to the physics award |website=physicsworld.com |date=5 October 2020 |access-date=2022-11-12}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 2003 Cirac was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2003&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> In 2017 he became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Ignacio Cirac |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ignacio-cirac/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

He has been granted many awards, notable ones being the 2006 [[Prince of Asturias Awards|Prince of Asturias Award]],<ref name="pda2006" /> the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/galardonados/ignacio-cirac-3/ |publisher=Fundación BBVA |title=Ignacio Cirac, Frontiers of Knowledge Laureate |access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref> in the Basic Sciences category ''ex aequo'' with [[Peter Zoller]], and [[The Franklin Institute]]'s 2010 [[The Franklin Institute Awards|Benjamin Franklin Medal]] in Physics (jointly with [[David J. Wineland]] and [[Peter Zoller]]). He was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] with Peter Zoller in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wolffund.org.il/index.php?dir=site&page=winners&cs=737&language=eng |title=Prof. Juan Ignacio Cirac Winner of Wolf Prize in Physics – 2013 |access-date=21 January 2018}}</ref> In 2018 he received the [[Max Planck Medal]] of the [[Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft|German Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mpq.mpg.de/5584519/17_11_23 |title=Prof. Ignacio Cirac receives Max-Planck Medal from the German Physical Society |author=Olivia Meyer-Streng |website=mpq.mpg.de|access-date=21 January 2018}}</ref> and the [[Micius Quantum Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/201904/28/WS5cc56cd8a3104842260b8e79.html |title=Chinese prize for quantum research announced |author=Zhu Lixin |work=China Daily|date=28 April 2019 |access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref> 

In 2023, he received the inaugural [[La Vanguardia Prize]] in the category "Innovation".<ref>{{Cite web |title=HomeActividades y Agenda - Entrega de la primera edición de los "Premios La Vanguardia" |url=https://casareal.es/ES/Actividades/Paginas/actividades_actividades_detalle.aspx?data=15867 |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=casareal.es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-09 |title=Ignacio Cirac receives first La Vanguardia Prize - presented by the King of Spain |url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/6901190/10-ignacio-cirac-la-vanguardia |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=www.mpq.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref> In 2026, he was awarded the [[Isaac Newton Medal]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/2026-isaac-newton-medal-and-lecture|title=2026 Isaac Newton Medal and Lecture: Professor J Ignacio Cirac|website=www.iop.org|access-date=12 October 2026}}</ref>
